pr.title: Add a testing guide and a write-tests skill
pr.head: c881dd7534dd12d7c73d03fa561a58ab19156e29

summary: Projector's skills write tests and judge them: implement adds tests to a change, fix-pr writes regression tests, and review-pr reads changed tests in its written-rules pass, the pass that checks a change against the rules a repository wrote down. Until now no skill said what makes a test worth keeping, so agents wrote tests such as one that asserts a default limit equals the literal the code sets it to. Such a test is a second copy of the source. It fails only when someone changes the value on purpose.

This pull request adds a testing guide, skills/testing.md, in ten numbered sections a review can cite as testing.md § 2. Its first rule is that each test must name the bug it catches: a plausible change that leaves the code wrong and turns the test red. A new section of the shared code guidelines, guidelines.md § 2, makes the guide a written rule, so a review flags a test that catches nothing as a blocking P2 finding. A new write-tests skill applies the guide on request, either to write tests for a change or to audit existing tests.
The change is all prose and packaging. No Python or TypeScript behavior changes; the one code edit adds the skill's name to the packaging test's published skill set.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Written-rules pass: the part of the review method that checks a change against skills/guidelines.md and the repository's own rule documents.
  • P2: a blocking review finding with bounded impact, or a break of a written rule. P3 is a non-blocking suggestion.
  • Skill: a folder under skills/ with a SKILL.md that Claude Code and Codex both load from the one tree.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One Projector review at c881dd7: clean, no finding threads.
  • One suggestion: say in guidelines.md § 2 which sections of testing.md a review files as P2.
  • The full gate passed: 1222 unit tests, project check, both claude plugin validate runs, claude plugin test ., and hooks/typecheck.sh.

groups.title: The testing guide
groups.kicker: Ten numbered rules for writing and judging tests
intro: skills/testing.md is a shared document beside writing.md and guidelines.md, not a skill of its own. Every skill that writes or judges tests reads it.

1. § 1 to § 4 say what a test is for and which tests catch nothing: restated values, tests of a mock, tests that cannot fail, coverage-only tests, change detectors, unread snapshots, and duplicates.
  2. § 5 to § 7 say where to aim tests, to test through the interface callers use, and to watch each new test fail by breaking the code it covers.
  3. § 8 to § 10 cover readable failures, a fast and deterministic suite, and deleting tests that catch nothing.

files.note: The guide itself. § 2 and § 3 carry the main argument: test what a value must agree with, not the literal.

checks.text: Pinning an exact value is still allowed when code outside the repository depends on it, such as an exit code that scripts check. Read this before you flag a literal assertion.

A test that stays green when the code is broken is a § 4 test. This matches the review method's rule that a finding needs a concrete failing sequence, so such a finding is reproducible. I read both documents side by side.

groups.title: Making the guide a written rule
groups.kicker: How implement, fix-pr, and the review method reach the guide
intro: guidelines.md holds the code rules that implement follows, fix-pr fixes against, and the review's written-rules pass enforces. A new § 2 points tests at the guide, so all three skills reach it through the file they already read.

The review method now tells the written-rules pass to read testing.md when a change adds or edits a test, and gives testing.md § 2 as a citation a finding can name. implement gets one sentence in its correctness check.

files.note: New § 2: judge tests by the guide, and file a test that catches nothing as a P2.

checks.text: The first paragraph says to judge tests by the whole guide, and this paragraph names a P2 only for a test that catches nothing. A break of another section alone, such as a vague test name under § 8, could read as either P2 or P3. The review left this as a suggestion.

files.note: The written-rules pass reads testing.md for changed tests and can cite its sections.
The correctness check now names the bug each test catches and watches it fail.

groups.title: The write-tests skill
groups.kicker: A skill that applies the guide on request
intro: write-tests has two modes. It writes tests for a change: list the bugs, cross off what no bug turns red, write each test, and watch it fail. Or it audits existing tests: keep, rewrite, or delete each one, and list the gaps. It commits nothing unless the user asks.

files.note: The skill. Each step cites the guide section that holds its rule.

checks.text: The frontmatter name matches the directory, which test_every_required_skill_has_matching_frontmatter_name checks; the test passed at this head.

files.note: Codex metadata, with the same three interface keys as the other skills.

groups.title: Listings and packaging
groups.kicker: Where the new skill is named
intro: Both plugin manifests publish the whole skills/ tree, so no manifest changes. The README, docs/plugins.md, and the packaging test are the places that list skills by name, and each gains write-tests.

files.note: Adds write-tests to the list of skills.
Lists the skill and says where the testing guide fits beside the code and writing guides.
Adds write-tests to PUBLISHED_SKILLS, which the test compares with the skills found on disk.
